Subtitle: Game music player
SupportInfo: You can support development on Ko-fi, if you wish.
BrowserError: Could not open the browser. https://ko-fi.com/roxyz0501
SearchHint: Search by track, duty or BGM ID
NoTracks: No matching tracks. Change the filters, or use a track’s + button to add it to a playlist.
CreatePlaylistFirst: Create a playlist on the left first.
MissingTracks: Keeping {0} tracks that are unavailable in the current game data.
VolumeInfo: 100% is the normal BGM level. You can raise it to 200%, up to the game’s volume limit. Game volume settings and sound effects are unchanged.
LockBgm: Ignore game BGM changes while playing
LockInfo: Applies to duty, battle and field music. When off, the next game BGM request restores normal music. Stopping, logging out or unloading also releases the override.
UseDuration: Use track durations for automatic advance
AdvanceInfo: Automatic advance uses an estimated duration, or the interval above when unknown. It does not detect the end of a track. Repeat one keeps the game’s original playback and looping behavior.
MoveInfo: Drag “BGMPlayer” at the top of the mini player to move it.
CatalogInfo: Tracks come from installed game data. Unknown titles are labeled “Untitled”, with a location when available. Unclassified tracks are under “Other”.
GameDataLanguage: Track and place names use the game data language. Supplementary track titles may be Japanese.
CommandHelp: /bgmplayer opens the player · /bgmplayer stop restores game music
VolumeHint: 100% is normal volume. Up to 200%, within the game’s limit. Sound effects, voices and ambient sounds are unchanged.
ApiUnavailable: BGM playback is unavailable. Check for game and Dalamud updates.
VolumeUnavailable: BGM volume control is unavailable. Check for game and Dalamud updates.
EngineNotReady: The BGM engine is not ready. Wait a moment, then try again.
TrackUnavailable: This track is not in the current game data.
PlaybackError: Playback failed. See the Dalamud log.
RestoreError: Could not restore game music. See the Dalamud log.
CatalogError: Could not load the track list. See the Dalamud log.
CatalogWarning: Some names or categories could not be loaded. Look under Other for unclassified tracks.
FontError: Some characters cannot be displayed. Check the optional language fonts in Windows.
